articles.headline: Premier League 'dragged through the mud' by Man City case - Gary Neville
articles.description: The Premier League has been "dragged through the mud" by the Manchester City guilty verdict, Gary Neville has said.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグはマンCの件で「泥を塗られた」― ゲイリー・ネヴィル
articles.descriptionJa: ゲイリー・ネヴィル氏は、マンチェスター・シティの有罪判決によってプレミアリーグが「泥を塗られた」と述べた。
articles.body:
The Premier League has been "dragged through the mud" by the Manchester City guilty verdict, Gary Neville has said.

An independent commission found City guilty on all charges related to breaching Premier League financial rules, concluding they "clearly intended to circumvent" the regulations over a period of nine seasons, primarily by disguising owner funding as sponsorship revenue.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher has called on the club's owner Sheikh Mansour to sell up, while former Manchester United full-back Neville believes the reputation of the whole league has been affected.

"To listen to this, it is chilling," he said on the Stick To Football podcast.

 

"We always think that we've got an enormous integrity, the Premier League, that we are the sort of league that sets the standard, and that it's other leagues that have got corruption, fraud, doping scandals, match-fixing, referee scandals.

"This is now coming to our country. This is now coming to our league. This is the greatest export that we have in our country. At the moment we're being dragged through the mud."

City were found to have inflated revenue and hid costs to the tune of more than £900 million ($1.1 billion) across the nine-season period, and in doing so avoided breaching Premier League and UEFA spending limits.

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Man City should be stripped of titles - Jamie Carragher

- Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy as an all-time coaching great?

They have indicated their intention to appeal against the commission's decision, saying it "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

City said "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all [the club's] positions."

Neville described the "irrefutable evidence" remark as "bizarre," adding: "It was a bit Trump-esque, wasn't it?"

articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
articles.description: The Steelers QB is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・ロジャースの2026年NFLシーズン：記録とマイルストーンを追う
articles.descriptionJa: スティーラーズのQBはNFL22年目のシーズンで記録更新に挑んでおり、ESPNは彼の「最後の挑戦」を記録している。
articles.body:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots.

"Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

Rodgers also went on to supplant Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in the second quarter of the Thursday night loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025.

But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 3 he has appeared in 290), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the fourth-most touchdown passes in NFL history (as of Week 3, he has 531) and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 3, he needs 3,026 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards. 

This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

Preseason: 0-for-0, 0 yards, 0 INTs, 0 sacks, 0 rushes

Despite early hints that Rodgers would take the field during the Steelers' first preseason under McCarthy, the veteran quarterback instead spent two games on the sideline and one on his couch at home. With Rodgers' top two receivers in DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. sidelined with preseason injuries, McCarthy opted to also keep his quarterback under wraps.

Rodgers isn't a stranger to sitting out the preseason in recent years. He didn't play in any preseason games for the Steelers in 2025, nor for the New York Jets in 2024 following his season-ending left Achilles tear in Week 1 of the 2023 season.

Week 1: Steelers 20, Falcons 13

Rodgers' stat line: 221 yards, 1 TD, 0 INTs, 2 sacks, 3 rushes for -1 yard

Rodgers didn't break any records this week, but he pulled within one touchdown pass of Peyton Manning for fourth most in NFL history with his second-quarter throw to tight end Pat Freiermuth for 6 yards. The touchdown toss was Rodgers' 232nd of the regular season. Rodgers had 26 pass attempts in the first half, his most attempts in the first half of a game since 2020 at Minnesota as a member of the Green Bay Packers, per ESPN Research.

articles.headline: Man City owners must sell due to 'shame of their guilt' - Jamie Carragher
articles.description: Manchester City's owners must sell up in the wake of the club's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.
articles.headlineJa: マンCオーナーは「有罪の恥」からクラブを売却すべき＝ジェイミー・キャラガー氏
articles.descriptionJa: 元リヴァプールのディフェンダー、ジェイミー・キャラガー氏によると、プレミアリーグの財務ルール違反による有罪判決を受け、マンチェスター・シティのオーナー陣はクラブを手放さなければならないという。
articles.body:
Manchester City's owners must sell up in the wake of the club's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.

Carragher says there can be no future for any executives implicated in the scandal, which City have stressed they intend to appeal, from majority owner Sheikh Mansour downwards.

An independent commission concluded City "clearly intended to circumvent Premier League rules" by inflating revenue and hiding costs through a series of "sham" commercial deals over a nine-season period.

Writing in the Daily Telegraph, Carragher said: "Manchester City are the end of their Abu Dhabi era. The club can only heal and recover from the shame of their guilt once the custodians recognise they have failed in their duty and sell up.

"There is no way to sugar-coat this. The scale of the institutional cheating and lack of co-operation in the investigation means the position of all City executives involved is untenable.

"Fighting on will only prolong the agony of supporters who wrong believe their pleas of innocence."

Carragher's views appear to contradict those of Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who suggested on Wednesday that such a sanction may not be suited to a group who have pumped billions into the club since their arrival in the city in 2008.

Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, told the BBC: "I would be really concerned to lose them.

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester. Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is."

Burnham's comments came after David Kogan, chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) said the ruling "raises serious issues" and pointed out the body has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives once proceedings come to a close.

Carragher is adamant there must be no mercy shown to those proven to have been complicit in one of the game's greatest controversies, and that any failure to uphold the rules will render such powers obsolete.

He added: "The Premier League's owners' and directors' test makes clear the repercussions for breaking the fundamental rules that all member clubs, including City, established and signed up to.

"Anyone who falls short must be disqualified from being Premier League directors and owners; otherwise, the regulations are not fit for purpose."

City have shown every intention of rigorously contesting the charges, and in a further development on Wednesday, the club's main sponsor Etihad Airways released a statement saying it was assessing its legal options following the independent commission's ruling.

articles.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: インターナショナルブレイク中に負傷したプレミアリーグの選手は？
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初のインターナショナルブレイク期間中に発生した、プレミアリーグのスター選手たちの負傷に関する最新ニュースと情報をお届けします。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.description: The Premier League is well underway, but with the transfer window closed, where do players stand in their teams? How deep do the squads go?
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ人気クラブの選手層一覧：鍵を握るのは誰？
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグは本格的に進行中ですが、移籍市場が閉じた今、各選手はチーム内でどのような立ち位置にいるのでしょうか？各クラブの選手層の厚さを検証します。
articles.body:
The Premier League season is five games in, and with the transfer window closed until Jan. 1, there will be no more incomings or outgoings (unless a free agent can be snapped up.)

As teams start to hit their stride and summer additions become accustomed to their surroundings, it's time to take a look at where the players stand with their respective squads.

Here are depth charts of the best options for the first XI and backup XI for the six most-followed clubs in the league. Of course, it's hard to predict who could be called upon as the fixtures pile up, but this should give you an idea of how strong each team is.

(Note: Each player appears in the main squad list once, even if he could fit into multiple spots. We have also included injured players, although those likely to be out for the season are noted separately.)

ARSENAL

Goalkeeper: David Raya, Kepa Arrizabalaga, Illan Meslier

Right back: Jurriën Timber, Ben White

Left back: Riccardo Calafiori, Piero Hincapié,

Center back: William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhães, Cristhian Mosquera, Ezri Konsa

Central midfield: Declan Rice, Martín Zubimendi, Bruno Guimarães, Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly

Attacking midfield/Forward: Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Eberechi Eze, Martin Ødegaard, 

Striker: Kai Havertz, Viktor Gyökeres

FIRST XI (4-2-3-1)

Raya

Timber, Saliba, Gabriel Magalhães, Calafiori

Rice, Guimarães

Saka, Ødegaard, Tzolis

Havertz

SECOND XI (4-3-3)

Kepa

White, Konsa, Mosquera, Hincapié

Lewis-Skelly, Merino

Madueke, Eze, Dowman

Gyökeres

EXTRAS: Meslier, Zubimendi

Arsenal came out of the summer window having executed their plans well. Those who departed were moved out largely on the club's terms, while the arrivals were clearly targeted according to specific requirements. The only slightly ambiguous outcome is that with the additions of defender Konsa and midfielder Guimarães, the Premier League champions have strengthened a core that was already exceptionally strong; Arteta might have to call on his man-management skills to keep certain players happy.

Konsa adds depth to an already impressive defense in the wake of an injury to William Saliba, while Guimarães does the same to central midfield as Zubimendi and Merino struggled for form and fitness respectively.

In attack, the club went through a mini-revamp. Four first-team players left -- Gabriel Jesus (Barcelona), Leandro Trossard (Besiktas), Gabriel Martinelli (Al Hilal) and Ethan Nwaneri (loan, Dortmund) -- while only one, Tzolis, arrived. The Greece international has made an encouraging start and gives Arteta a different option from the left, with a superb right foot and set-piece expertise, and while Eze and Madueke can deputize there, Tzolis is the only specialist in the role. Using either of the former two on the left may also reduce the cover available elsewhere, particularly for the injury-prone Ødegaard. articles.headline: Sources: Steelers to trade Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys
articles.description: The Steelers agreed to trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources confirmed to ESPN on Wednesday night.
articles.headlineJa: 情報筋：スティーラーズがジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアをカウボーイズへトレード
articles.descriptionJa: スティーラーズがコーナーバックのジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアを2027年のドラフト6巡目指名権および2028年の2巡目指名権との交換でカウボーイズへトレードすることに合意したと、水曜夜に複数の情報筋がESPNに明かしました。
articles.body:
After a lengthy and contentious contract standoff and a lingering back issue, Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. is going to the Dallas Cowboys.

The Steelers on Wednesday night agreed to trade Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder, sources told ESPN. 

The trade marks the end of a monthslong saga that stretched throughout the Steelers' offseason as Porter, one of the team's 2023 second-round picks, awaited an extension and was sidelined by a back injury.

The heart of the dispute was the guaranteed money within the contract's structure, sources told ESPN, and the sides never made meaningful progress on agreeing to terms despite talks as late as hours before kickoff of the Steelers' Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers then stopped talks because they don't negotiate during the regular season as a longstanding organizational principle.

Porter, who started 41 games and had three interceptions in three seasons, sat out all of the team's training camp and preseason after reporting an aggravation to the back injury during the team's mobility workout on the first day of camp. He was put on the physically unable to perform list until roster cutdown day in late August.

Porter was then a limited participant in every regular-season practice until earlier this week as coach Mike McCarthy said the cornerback was progressing through a "ramp-up" phase during the first month of the season.

Porter was inactive for each of the first three games and had been ruled out earlier Wednesday of the Steelers' game Thursday night against the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers added a back injury to Wednesday's practice report in addition to the "not injury related-conditioning" description the team used for Porter's injury status for most of the past three weeks. Porter had previously been a full participant in the team's Monday and Tuesday walkthroughs.

His departure means the Steelers will continue to operate with Asante Samuel Jr., Jamel Dean and Daylen Everette rotating at outside cornerback. Everette, a 2026 third-round draft pick, played extended snaps in a Week 3 win against the Cincinnati Bengals, first coming in for a briefly injured Dean and then replacing Samuel for much of the second half.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones hinted during training camp that he would be willing to give up draft capital to help this season's team. Jones was asked on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas on Monday about a potential trade with reports of the team's interest in Porter.

While not specifically talking about Porter because of tampering rules, Jones said, "I'd just say we're right on top of it. We're very aware of the moving parts out here."

articles.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys, J.J. McCarthy to Giants
articles.description: Can Joey Porter Jr. clean up the Cowboys' defense? Will J.J. McCarthy improve the Giants' QB situation? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
articles.headlineJa: NFLトレード期限の移籍評価：ジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアがカウボーイズへ、J・J・マッカーシーがジャイアンツへ
articles.descriptionJa: ジョーイ・ポーター・ジュニアはカウボーイズの守備陣を立て直すことができるでしょうか？J・J・マッカーシーはジャイアンツのQB事情を改善できるでしょうか？11月のトレード期限を前に、NFLのトレードを採点・評価します。
articles.body:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, which will pass on Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for the first two deals of trading season: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants and Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys. Check back right through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Steelers trade CB Porter to Cowboys

Cowboys get: CB Joey Porter Jr.

Steelers get: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Cowboys grade: B

Steelers grade: C+

This is the Cowboys' third trade with the Steelers in the past 18 months (George Pickens and Broderick Jones), and it's their third trade involving a star defensive player after acquiring Quinnen Williams at the trade deadline last season and shipping Micah Parsons to Green Bay last offseason.

It's easy to see what the Cowboys are doing here. DaRon Bland, who first broke onto the scene as a slot corner, was playing on the outside given Dallas' lack of depth. By acquiring Porter, Bland can move back inside, which will allow the Cowboys to relocate 2026 first-round defensive back Caleb Downs, as well. He has been playing the slot, but his natural position is at safety. These are options, not guarantees. Bland might stay outside as the Cowboys instead pursue a strong 1-2 punch at outside corner, with Porter shadowing WR1s.

The salient point is this: Porter can have a rising tide impact on the Cowboys secondary, clarifying the roles of other players and enhancing the whole unit in the process.

Porter is not as tricky of a scheme fit in Dallas as people think, too. His strengths are certainly his length and physicality, such that he can line up in press -- but he has been in press alignments on only 30.6% of his snaps over his career, just above the league average for cornerbacks (24.1%). Porter is a much better man coverage defender than he is in zone, as his passer rating allowed in man coverage over the past four seasons is better than all but Derek Stingley Jr. But the Cowboys are actually running more man coverage (24.8%) under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker than the league average (23.2%) over the first three weeks.

Of course, early-season rate stats can be noisy. Parker's Vic Fangio-inspired defense will require Porter to play from greater depth than he did in Pittsburgh, and the communication and keys required in that match-heavy system will take some getting used to. articles.headline: Former Steelers HC Mike Tomlin reveals massive Minecraft city
articles.description: The former Steelers coach revealed an unexpected longtime hobby that shocked the sports and gaming worlds.
articles.headlineJa: 元スティーラーズHCのマイク・トムリン、マインクラフトの巨大都市を披露
articles.descriptionJa: 元スティーラーズのヘッドコーチが意外な長年の趣味を明かし、スポーツ界とゲーム界を驚かせました。
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin is a Super Bowl-winning head coach, is second on the Pittsburgh Steelers' all-time wins list and famously never had a losing record in 19 seasons with the Steelers.

But on Wednesday, Tomlin showed a side of himself rarely seen: that of an architect. On Minecraft, to be exact.

Speaking about his passions for high-rise buildings and urban planning, Tomlin unveiled his Minecraft world in a nearly 20-minute YouTube video. Tomlin has been working on the ongoing project for 12-plus years.

After he watched his kids obsessively play the game in middle school, Tomlin became intrigued by the game's creative mode, which allows users to build cities with unlimited resources. The former head coach explains on the video that he likes to build and always had an interest in architecture.

It also became a way for Tomlin to spend time with his kids. Each of them participated and have buildings across the city.

"Over the course of time, they got just disinterested in the game. They go on to high school and so forth and off to college. Their participation became less and less over the years. My participation probably at times increased," Tomlin says, laughing. "At different times over the course of a 12-month calendar, I would have different levels of fixation on this."

He remembers constructing the various communities, neighborhoods and buildings with challenges along the way. But he describes the process of building his world as "mindless entertainment" and "therapeutic."

"I'm not a big TV watcher," he says. "It allowed me to detach from the realities and the pressures of life."

Tomlin shows off the various apartments and architecture, and he gives a tour of buildings, apologizing for his "lack of stick control" with a controller.

He also breaks down his vision for the city: densely populated buildings around a body of water. He started small before building neighborhoods over 12 years.

The first building Tomlin created is a "boutique hotel" that includes an executive spa and therapy rooms. He described himself as "lighting conscious" when building it, using glass ceilings when appropriate. The hotel includes indoor and outdoor boutiques, an elevator well and a main desk.

Another community within his city features an apartment building with an aquarium on each floor.

He says he was "view conscious" of the many high rises, making sure the high-end urban apartment buildings had great sightlines. One of them is right across from baseball and soccer stadiums, which Tomlin teases he'll reveal in another episode.

No detail was too small.

"You'll find appropriate number of public restrooms and stuff throughout all my public facilities, men's and women's restrooms," he says. "Not anything over the top in terms of detail ... but it was important that I represented that."
